heading: EXT. SALT DESERT - GENERATION SHIP HULL - DAWN

units.text: EXT. SALT DESERT - GENERATION SHIP HULL - DAWN
A ship the size of a mountain lies on its side in a white plain of salt.
Its hull, once silver, is rust-red and blistered.
Cables hang like dead vines.
The sky is a bruised violet.
Two moons, one faint, one bright.
At the foot of the hull, a rope ladder dangles.
Beyond it, a gaping breach, dark as a throat.
IXCHEL, 30s, wiry, wrapped in a patchwork cloak the color of dust, scales the ladder one handhold at a time.
A pack of glass tubes clinks on her back.
Her face is scarred with the faint blue lines of old ship-tattoos, a map no one living can read.
At the top, she hauls herself into the breach.
Waits for her eyes to adjust.
AMADI, 60s, sits cross-legged in the shadows, so still he seems part of the wall.
His skin is dark, his head shaved, his eyes the pale green of old copper.
A single lantern glows beside him, powered by something that hums.
You're real.
units.name: IXCHEL

units.text: So are you.
units.name: AMADI

units.text: They said the last one died.
units.name: IXCHEL

units.text: They say many things.
units.name: AMADI

units.text: She steps closer.
The floor, once a corridor, is now a slope of salt-crusted tile.
I came to see the Bridge.
units.name: IXCHEL

units.text: The Bridge is gone.
units.name: AMADI

units.text: The maps say --
units.name: IXCHEL

units.text: Maps were written by people who left.
units.name: AMADI

units.text: She sets down her pack.
Kneels.
He studies her tattoos with open interest, like a man reading a letter from a village he forgot.
Whose line are you?
units.name: AMADI

units.text: The Surveyors.
units.name: IXCHEL

units.text: Ah. They always came back for a last measurement.
units.name: AMADI

units.text: We came back for the seeds.
units.name: IXCHEL

units.text: There are no seeds.
units.name: AMADI

units.text: There must be.
units.name: IXCHEL

units.text: There was a garden. Then there was a long winter. Then there was me.
units.name: AMADI

units.text: He lifts the lantern.
The light sweeps a wall, and she sees it: a mural of green, thousands of tiny painted leaves, fading but not gone.
You painted this.
units.name: IXCHEL

units.text: Every day, for forty years.
units.name: AMADI

units.text: Why?
units.name: IXCHEL

units.text: So that someone would come and see a garden.
units.name: AMADI

units.text: She touches the wall.
Her hand leaves a dark print in the dust.
Then, slowly, she opens the pack and begins unpacking her glass tubes: soil, water, a single vial of grain.
Then let me plant what you remember.
units.name: IXCHEL

units.text: Amadi does not answer.
He lowers the lantern and begins, very slowly, to weep.
